record.paper_title: Conjectures and Open Questions on the Structure and Regularity of Spaces with Lower Ricci Curvature Bounds
record.original_question: Let (X, d, p) be a noncollapsed lower-Ricci limit obtained as a Gromov–Hausdorff limit of pointed Riemannian manifolds (M_i^n, g_i, p_i) with Ric ≥ −λ and Vol(B_1(p_i)) > v > 0. For the Federer stratification S^k(X) = {x ∈ X : no tangent cone at x is (k+1)-symmetric}, is S^k(X) contained in a union of k-dimensional submanifolds in the following sense: there exists a countable collection of bi-Hölder maps φ_i : B_1(0^k) → M such that, if Ŝ^k(X) = ⋃_i φ_i(B_1(0^k)), then S^k(X) ⊆ Ŝ^k(X) and every tangent cone at each x ∈ Ŝ^k(X) is at least k-symmetric?

evidence.quote: Definition 2.11 (stratification). We define the k-stratum Sk(X) ⊆ X by Sk(X) ≡ {x ∈ X : no tangent cone at x is k + 1-symmetric}.

Conjecture 2.15. Let Mni, gi, pi → (X, d, p) satisfy Ric ≥ −λ and Vol(B1(pi)) > v > 0, then Sk is contained in a union of k-dimensional submanifolds. More precisely, there exist a countable collection of bi-Hölder maps ϕi : B1(0k) → M such that if Ŝk(X) ≡ ⋃i ϕi(B1(0k)) then 1) Sk(X) ⊆ Ŝk(X), 2) for each x ∈ Ŝk(X) we have that every tangent cone is at least k-symmetric.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 2$, $\lambda\ge 0$, and $v>0$ be fixed. Suppose $(M_i^n,g_i,p_i)$ is a sequence of pointed complete Riemannian $n$-manifolds satisfying
\[\mathrm{Ric}_{g_i}\ge -\lambda\,g_i\qquad\text{and}\qquad \mathrm{Vol}(B_1(p_i))>v,\]
and that $(M_i^n,g_i,p_i)$ converges in the pointed Gromov–Hausdorff sense to a pointed metric space $(X,d,p)$ (a noncollapsed lower-Ricci limit).

For $x\in X$, a tangent cone at $x$ is any pointed Gromov–Hausdorff limit of rescalings $(X,r_i^{-1}d,x)$ with $r_i\downarrow 0$. A pointed metric space $(Y,d_Y,y)$ is called $k$-symmetric if it is isometric to $(\mathbb{R}^k\times C(Z),d_{\mathrm{prod}},(0,o_C))$ for some compact metric space $Z$, where $C(Z)$ is the metric cone over $Z$ with vertex $o_C$. Define the Federer-type stratification
\[S^k(X)\;=\;\{x\in X:\text{no tangent cone at }x\text{ is }(k+1)\text{-symmetric}\},\qquad k=0,1,\dots,n-1.\]

A map $\varphi:B_1(0^k)\subset\mathbb{R}^k\to X$ is bi-Hölder if there exist $\alpha\in(0,1]$ and $C>0$ such that
\[C^{-1}|u-v|^{1/\alpha}\le d(\varphi(u),\varphi(v))\le C\,|u-v|^{\alpha}\qquad\text{for all }u,v\in B_1(0^k).\]

Decide whether the following statement holds for every such limit $(X,d,p)$ and every $0\le k\le n-1$: there exists a countable collection of bi-Hölder maps $\varphi_i:B_1(0^k)\to X$ such that, setting
\[\widehat S^k(X)\;=\;\bigcup_i \varphi_i(B_1(0^k)),\]
one has
\begin{enumerate}
\item $S^k(X)\subseteq \widehat S^k(X)$, and
\item for every $x\in \widehat S^k(X)$, every tangent cone of $X$ at $x$ is at least $k$-symmetric.
\end{enumerate}
artifact.category_tag: Ricci limit spaces and singular strata
artifact.status_search_result: Cheeger–Jiang–Naber (Annals of Mathematics, 2021) established that each stratum $S^k$ of a noncollapsed Ricci limit is $k$-rectifiable, which is a measure-theoretic version of the conjecture. The stronger statement requested here — covering $S^k$ by bi-Hölder images of $k$-dimensional Euclidean balls whose union $\widehat S^k$ consists entirely of points with at least $k$-symmetric tangent cones — appears not to be established in full generality. Thus the conjecture is partially solved (rectifiability) but the bi-Hölder manifold-cover formulation is still open as of recent literature.

status_evidence.title: Rectifiability of singular sets of noncollapsed limit spaces with Ricci curvature bounded below
status_evidence.snippet: S^k is k-rectifiable for all k in noncollapsed Ricci limit spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Rectifiability (a weaker form of the conjecture) is established.

status_evidence.title: Rectifiability of Singular Sets in Noncollapsed Spaces with Ricci Curvature bounded below
status_evidence.snippet: Main theorem proves k-rectifiability of S^k via bi-Lipschitz parametrizations on subsets of positive measure, not bi-Hölder covers giving the symmetry conclusion on the entire union.
status_evidence.claim: Bi-Lipschitz/rectifiability results exist; the conjectured bi-Hölder cover with tangent-cone symmetry on the whole union is stronger.
